summary_en: This study tests a dietary intervention for people with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma who are receiving induction chemotherapy with daratumumab (or isatuximab), lenalidomide, bortezomib, and dexamethasone (DRVd). The intervention group receives high-fiber plant-based meals for 12 weeks and dietitian phone or video calls every 2 weeks for 12 weeks, while the usual care group has study team calls every 4 weeks and one dietitian call at the end of induction chemotherapy. The study measures quality of life using questionnaires, and it also looks at treatment response and other disease, microbiome, and immune markers.
summary_es: Este estudio evalúa una intervención dietética para personas con mieloma múltiple recién diagnosticado que reciben quimioterapia de inducción con daratumumab (o isatuximab), lenalidomida, bortezomib y dexametasona (DRVd). El grupo de intervención recibe comidas basadas en plantas y ricas en fibra durante 12 semanas, y llamadas o videollamadas con un dietista cada 2 semanas durante 12 semanas; el grupo de atención habitual tiene llamadas con el equipo del estudio cada 4 semanas y una llamada con un dietista al final de la quimioterapia de inducción. El estudio mide la calidad de vida mediante cuestionarios, y también analiza la respuesta al tratamiento y otros marcadores de la enfermedad, del microbioma e inmunológicos.
who_for: Newly diagnosed multiple myeloma with bone marrow involvement, age 18 or older.
Planned four 28-day cycles of DRVd induction chemotherapy.
Baseline dietary fiber intake under 30 grams per day on a 24-hour recall.
Not following a minimally processed whole-food plant-based diet in the last 3 months.
Able to complete study surveys, procedures and visits.
not_for: Leptomeningeal or central nervous system involvement.
Body mass index of 19 or lower.
Severe allergy to legumes, peanuts or tree nuts.
Prior combination infusion chemotherapy such as VDPACE or DCEP.
Concurrent weight loss or dietary program that requires a specific diet or weight loss supplements.
